scope: Source-only QA alternative. No deployment or hosted schema change. Synthetic SQL, RPC and HTTP inputs.

tests.name: event_sql
cases: installation is disabled and does not replay historical events
private jobs remain inaccessible even though the provider queue stays readable
queued data contains only an opaque job and one short-lived event capability
an observed token cannot select another event, recipient, body or SQL operation
atomic claim and completion fence duplicate requests and stale acknowledgements
expired and paused event capabilities do not dispatch
legacy mode enabled after enqueue prevents claiming and after claim prevents forwarding
pause and expiry after claim prevent a fresh forward but do not prevent final acknowledgement
deleted notifications and deactivated recipients cannot consume a capability
canceled calls and revoked initiating sessions cannot consume a capability
ringing calls map only to the canonical call and never ordinary incoming-call pushes
current call authorization still rejects a session revoked after the event claim
group call insertion commits invitations together before one queued call is consumed
outbox uniqueness prevents re-enqueue and existing legacy mode prevents double dispatch
queue failure preserves the app event and cannot produce a usable failed capability
operator retention is bounded, keeps recent jobs and preserves canonical notifications

tests.name: event_handler
cases: canonical DB claim controls the fixed target and all outgoing fields
only a canonical call claim selects the call endpoint
arbitrary routing, recipient, body, credential and SQL fields fail before privileged lookup
expired, stale and replayed claims never reach the downstream service
a pause or legacy-mode switch after claim prevents forwarding, but still records the skip
an unavailable recheck records uncertainty instead of forwarding or reusing the token
invalid DB receipts cannot choose another target or an arbitrary event
production and missing service configuration are refused before any claim
method and body size bounds reject oversized inputs without dispatch
uncertain provider outcomes remain one-shot and never echo sensitive failure bodies
recipient skip and provider rejection are persisted with exact terminal outcomes
failed acknowledgement never reports completion or retries the forward call
cancellation before lookup or while the claim result is uncertain never forwards
cancellation during forwarding records uncertainty using an independent acknowledgement deadline

tests.name: existing_push_handlers
cases: ordinary push refuses anonymous, anon-key and user JWT callers before any database or provider access
a service webhook can deliver only the stored notification, ignoring forged recipient, type, text and routing
missing, expired, muted and quiet-hour notifications do not reach a provider
both Expo token formats work, duplicate registrations send once and unknown badges do not clear the icon
Expo batches never exceed100, and a revocation prevents later batches
provider errors and malformed tickets are never counted as delivered or accepted
DeviceNotRegistered cleanup names the original owner, token and registration timestamp
call ringing requires a verified nonanonymous user and live caller authorization
a caller cannot ring someone else call, an ended call or an expired call
call push respects master/category/quiet preferences and requires the database dispatch claim
database trigger and client races acquire only one recipient dispatch and produce one ring
revocation during preparation stops ringing before the provider sees a request
recipient removal after the claim prevents both trusted and user-initiated rings
recipient revocation between provider batches stops the later devices
APNs uses the QA topic, explicit environment, original CallKit UUID and immediate expiration
missing APNs credentials cannot prevent an eligible Android receiver from ringing
APNs rejection is reported and does not retry a token against a different environment
provider timeout is bounded and records an uncertain attempt without blindly sending again

officialClassifier.reason: Explicit bounded operator retention DELETE remains unchanged and visible.

limits: An observer of the provider queue can advance the existing authorized event; a queue writer can suppress it. No arbitrary recipient/body/route is accepted.
A feature switch after the downstream request begins cannot retract it. Mode switching requires pausing, draining, and inspecting in-flight/unknown jobs.
At-most-once forwarding can lose an attempt after claim if the worker crashes. It intentionally avoids blind replay after an unknown provider outcome.
The candidate still requires reviewed hosted installation, exact Edge readbacks, request limiting, an operator retention schedule and disposable-event/provider/installed-device acceptance.
The pending business-auth connector invocation did not return an outcome. No new hosted mutation is authorized by this receipt.
